title: Huevos Rancheros-Style Breakfast Plates with Make-Ahead Ranchero Sauce and Pinto Beans
description: Cook the chile-tomato sauce and seasoned pintos on Sunday; each morning, crisp two corn tortillas and fry an egg. About $1 a plate for six breakfasts.
notes: The sauce and beans are the make-ahead part: portion each into six small containers and refrigerate within 2 hours, where they keep 5 days. Both freeze well for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator or loosen in a covered saucepan with a splash of water. Cook the eggs each morning, since fried eggs turn rubbery when frozen and reheated. Reheat sauce and beans until steaming hot (165°F) before building the plate. Seed the jalapeño for a mild sauce, or leave the seeds in for heat. A sprinkle of crumbled block feta or shredded Monterey Jack is a good addition, but it adds milk and the plate is no longer dairy-free. Corn tortillas keep 2 weeks in the refrigerator and freeze for 2 months in their bag.

ingredients.name: pinto beans (15 oz each), with their liquid
lime, cut into wedges, for serving

instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring now and then, until soft and turning golden at the edges, 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic and jalapeño and cook 1 minute more, until fragrant.

Pour in the tomatoes with their juice and add 1/2 teaspoon of the cumin, the oregano, and 3/4 teaspoon of the salt. Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and the raw tomato taste is gone.
Blend the sauce until mostly smooth with a few small bits left, using an immersion blender in the pan or a countertop blender with the lid vented. Taste and add salt if needed.

Meanwhile, tip the pinto beans and their liquid into a small saucepan with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon cumin and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Simmer over medium-low for 8 to 10 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans with a fork or spoon, until thick and creamy.
Cool the sauce and beans, portion each into six containers, and refrigerate or freeze. To serve, reheat one portion of each until steaming hot.

Warm a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat with a few drops of the remaining oil. Heat two tortillas at a time, 30 to 45 seconds per side, until spotty brown and pliable or as crisp as you like. Stack them on a plate.

Lower the heat to medium, add a little more oil, and crack in an egg. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the white is fully set and the yolk is done the way you like it; cover the pan for the last minute to set the top.
Overlap the two tortillas on a plate, spread with the beans, set the egg on top, and spoon the hot ranchero sauce around it. Finish with cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Tamagoyaki-Style Rolled Omelet for the Week
description: Thin layers of lightly sweet, soy-seasoned egg rolled into two neat logs and sliced for breakfasts and lunch boxes. Eight eggs make four servings at about 70 cents each.
equipment: rectangular tamagoyaki pan or 8-inch nonstick skillet
bamboo sushi mat or plastic wrap
notes: A rectangular pan gives square slices, but a round 8-inch skillet works: trim the rounded ends after rolling and eat them as the cook's share. Keep the heat at medium; too hot and the layers brown and turn spongy, too low and they will not stick together. Wrapped tightly, the rolls keep 4 days in the refrigerator, and slices are good cold, at room temperature in a lunch box for up to 2 hours, or warmed briefly. To freeze, wrap sliced portions in plastic, bag them, and freeze up to 1 month; thaw overnight in the refrigerator, and expect a slightly softer texture. Use gluten-free tamari in place of soy sauce for a gluten-free roll; it still contains soy. Stir 2 thinly sliced scallions into the eggs for a savory version. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking and reheat to 165°F if serving hot.

ingredients.name: hot cooked jasmine rice, for serving

instructions: Crack the eggs into a bowl and add the water, sugar, mirin, soy sauce, and salt. Beat with chopsticks or a fork, cutting through the whites rather than whipping, until no streaks remain but the mixture is not foamy. Divide it evenly between two measuring cups, one for each roll.

Pour the oil into a small dish and fold a paper towel into a pad. Heat the pan over medium heat, then wipe it with the oiled towel. Test with a drop of egg: it should sizzle gently and set within a few seconds.

Pour in about a quarter of the first cup of egg and tilt the pan to coat the bottom thinly. Prick any large bubbles. When the layer is set at the edges but still slightly wet on top, about 1 minute, roll it from the far end toward you in three or four folds.

Push the roll back to the far end of the pan and wipe the empty space with the oiled towel. Pour in another quarter of the egg, lift the roll so the new egg runs underneath it, and when it is nearly set, roll the log back toward you, wrapping it in the new layer.

Repeat with the rest of the first cup, oiling the pan between layers, until you have a firm, even log with no liquid egg inside, 6 to 8 minutes in all. Slide it onto a bamboo mat or a sheet of plastic wrap and roll snugly to square the shape.
Wipe the pan, oil it, and make the second roll with the remaining egg. Let both rolls rest in their wraps for 5 minutes to set the shape.
Cut each roll into 8 slices with a sharp knife. Serve warm with rice, or cool completely, wrap, and refrigerate or freeze in portions.

title: Sheet-Pan Egg and Cheddar Breakfast Sandwiches for the Freezer
description: A dozen eggs baked in one pan with peppers and scallions, cut into squares, and stacked on English muffins with cheddar. Twelve grab-and-go sandwiches for about 90 cents each.
notes: The eggs are done when the center no longer jiggles and a knife slid in comes out clean; overbaking makes them tough, so start checking at 15 minutes. Refrigerate assembled sandwiches within 2 hours; they keep 4 days. To freeze, wrap each one in parchment or foil, bag, and freeze up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen: unwrap, wrap in a paper towel, microwave at half power for 1 1/2 minutes, flip, then microwave at full power 30 to 60 seconds until the center reaches 165°F. Swap the cheddar for Monterey Jack or American cheese, or add a slice of deli turkey breast to each sandwich; neither changes the allergens. Use a dairy-free cheese and plant milk to make them dairy-free. Leftover egg squares are also good chopped into fried rice or tucked into a tortilla.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, softened, for the pan
English muffins or burger buns, split

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Line a 13 x 18-inch rimmed sheet pan with parchment, letting it come up the sides, and rub the parchment with the softened butter.

Whisk the eggs, milk, salt, and several grinds of pepper in a large bowl until completely smooth with no streaks of white. Pour into the pan and scatter the bell pepper and scallions evenly over the top.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, rotating the pan halfway, until the center is set, springs back when pressed, and a knife comes out clean.
Sprinkle the cheddar evenly over the hot eggs and return the pan to the oven for 1 to 2 minutes, just until the cheese melts. Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, toast the English muffins in batches in a toaster or on a second sheet pan in the oven for 5 to 7 minutes, until lightly crisp.
Lift the eggs out on the parchment and cut into 12 even squares, three cuts the long way and two the short way. Fold any edges under so each square fits its muffin.
Set a square of egg on each muffin bottom and cap with the top. Serve right away, or cool completely and wrap individually for the refrigerator or freezer.

title: Savory Ginger Oatmeal with Soft-Cooked Egg and Scallion
description: Rolled oats simmered in broth with ginger, garlic, and peas, finished with soy sauce, sesame oil, and a jammy egg. A warming porridge breakfast for about 85 cents a bowl.
notes: Soft-cooked eggs keep 4 days in the refrigerator in their shells or peeled in a covered container, so a batch on Sunday covers most of the week. The oatmeal keeps 5 days refrigerated and freezes well for up to 2 months in single portions; thaw overnight or microwave from frozen, stirring every minute. It thickens as it cools, so add 1/4 cup water or broth per bowl when reheating, and heat until steaming (165°F). Do not freeze the eggs, since the whites turn rubbery. Use certified gluten-free oats and gluten-free tamari in place of the soy sauce to make it gluten-free; it still contains soy. Chile crisp, a handful of baby spinach stirred in at the end, or a little leftover shredded chicken all fit here. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated

instructions: Bring a medium saucepan of water to a boil. Lower the cold eggs in gently with a slotted spoon and cook at a steady simmer for 7 minutes for a jammy yolk. Move them to a bowl of ice water for at least 5 minutes, then peel or refrigerate in the shell.
Heat the neutral oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the ginger, garlic, and the white parts of the scallions and cook, stirring, for about 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in the oats and toast them for 1 minute. Add the broth, water, and salt, raise the heat, and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until the oats are soft and the porridge is loose and creamy.
Stir in the frozen peas and cook 2 minutes more, until they are bright green and hot. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the soy sauce and half the sesame oil. Taste for salt.

Ladle into bowls, halve an egg over each, and finish with the scallion greens, a few drops of the remaining sesame oil, and red pepper flakes if you like. To prep ahead, cool the oatmeal and portion it into containers, keeping the eggs and scallions separate.

title: Banana Oat Blender Pancakes for the Freezer
description: Rolled oats, ripe banana, eggs, and milk whizzed into a batter in the blender, with no flour needed. A double stack freezes well and toasts back in minutes, about 50 cents a serving.
notes: The 10-minute rest lets the oats absorb liquid so the pancakes hold together; if the batter gets too thick to pour after sitting, blend in a tablespoon or two of milk. Very ripe, heavily freckled bananas give the most sweetness, so the batter needs no sugar. Standard rolled oats work if gluten is not a concern; certified gluten-free oats keep the recipe gluten-free. Use unsweetened nut-free plant milk and oil for the pan to make them dairy-free. Cooled pancakes keep 4 days in the refrigerator. To freeze, lay them in a single layer on a baking sheet until firm, about 1 hour, then bag them with parchment between stacks for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in a toaster on a low setting, or microwave two pancakes for 45 to 60 seconds until hot through. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

ingredients.name: certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (180 g)
mashed very ripe banana (about 2 medium, 225 g)
melted butter, plus more for the pan

instructions: Blend the oats on high for 30 to 45 seconds, until they are a fine, flour-like powder.

Add the banana, eggs, milk, baking powder, cinnamon, salt, vanilla, and melted butter. Blend until completely smooth, scraping down the sides once, about 30 seconds. Let the batter rest in the blender jar for 10 minutes to thicken.

Heat a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium heat until a drop of water sizzles, then brush lightly with butter. Pour in 1/4-cup portions of batter, leaving room between them, and drop a few blueberries onto each if using.
Cook until the edges look set and small bubbles appear on top, 2 to 3 minutes; banana batter browns faster than plain batter, so lower the heat if the undersides darken before the bubbles show.
Flip carefully with a thin spatula and cook 1 1/2 to 2 minutes more, until the center springs back when pressed. Move to a wire rack, butter the pan again, and repeat with the remaining batter.
Serve warm, or cool the pancakes completely on the rack before refrigerating or freezing so they do not steam and stick together.

title: Sinangag-Style Filipino Garlic Fried Rice with Fried Eggs and Tomato Salad
description: Day-old rice fried in plenty of toasted garlic, topped with a crisp-edged egg and a sharp tomato and shallot salad, the way many Filipino breakfasts begin. About 75 cents a plate.
equipment: 12-inch nonstick or well-seasoned skillet or wok
notes: Cold rice is the key: freshly cooked rice steams and clumps, while rice that has rested a night in the refrigerator separates into crisp grains. Cooked rice needs care, so cool it quickly, refrigerate within 1 hour if you can and never more than 2, and use it within 4 days. The garlic rice keeps 4 days refrigerated and freezes up to 2 months in flat bags; reheat in a skillet or microwave, covered with a damp paper towel, until steaming hot (165°F). Fry the eggs fresh each morning, which takes 3 minutes, since fried eggs do not freeze well. In the Philippines this plate is called silog when served with a meat, such as tapa or longganisa; a browned ground turkey patty cooked to 165°F is a budget stand-in. A splash of distilled vinegar with chopped garlic makes a traditional dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: cold cooked jasmine rice (about 640 g), from the day before

instructions: Stir the tomatoes, shallot, vinegar, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt together in a small bowl and set aside while you cook; the shallot softens and the juices turn into a light dressing.

Put 2 tablespoons of the oil and the garlic in a cold 12-inch skillet or wok and set it over medium-low heat. Cook, stirring often, for 4 to 6 minutes, until the garlic is evenly golden and smells toasty. Spoon out about a third of the garlic onto a plate for topping; it will crisp as it cools.

Break up the cold rice with your hands so there are no clumps. Raise the heat to medium-high, add the rice to the garlic oil, and sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and a few grinds of pepper.

Stir-fry for 5 to 7 minutes, pressing the rice against the pan and then tossing, until every grain is coated, hot through, and some are lightly crisp. Taste for salt and move the rice to plates or containers.

Wipe the pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, and heat over medium-high. Crack in the eggs and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning a little hot oil over the whites, until the whites are set with lacy brown edges and the yolks are done the way you like them.
Top each plate of rice with an egg, the reserved toasted garlic, and scallions if using, and serve the tomato salad on the side.

title: Mixed Berry Chia Pudding Jars with Maple and Vanilla
description: Chia seeds set overnight in plant milk with maple and vanilla, layered with a quick compote from frozen berries. Four ready jars for the week at about 95 cents each, no cooking skill required.
notes: Whisk twice, once at the start and again after 10 minutes, or the seeds settle into a solid clump at the bottom. The pudding needs at least 4 hours in the refrigerator to set and is best after a night. Assembled jars keep 5 days refrigerated. Chia pudding can be frozen in jars, leaving an inch of headspace, for up to 1 month; thaw overnight in the refrigerator and stir well, as it will be a little looser. The berry compote freezes on its own for 3 months. Whole milk or plain whole-milk yogurt can stand in for the plant milk, which adds milk and makes the jars no longer vegan or dairy-free. Oat milk is a good choice; use unsweetened certified gluten-free oat milk if anyone avoids gluten. Check the plant milk label: soy milk adds soy, and almond milk adds tree nuts. Honey works in place of maple syrup, though the jars are then not vegan.

ingredients.name: hemp hearts or raw pumpkin seeds, for topping

instructions: Whisk the chia seeds, plant milk, 2 tablespoons of the maple syrup, the vanilla, and the salt in a medium bowl until no clumps of seeds remain.
Let the mixture stand for 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up any seeds that have settled. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight, until thick and spoonable.

Meanwhile, put the frozen berries, the remaining 1 tablespoon maple syrup, and the lemon juice in a small saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring and pressing some berries with a spoon, for 6 to 8 minutes, until juicy and slightly thickened. Cool completely.
Stir the set pudding, then layer it in four jars with the berry compote, starting and ending with pudding or with a spoonful of fruit on top.
Lid the jars and refrigerate. Add hemp hearts or pumpkin seeds just before eating so they stay crisp.

title: Balila-Style Warm Chickpeas with Cumin, Garlic, and Lemon
description: A Levantine breakfast of chickpeas warmed in their own liquid, then dressed with garlic, cumin, lemon, and olive oil and scooped up with pita. About $1.50 a bowl, and the beans freeze well.
equipment: mortar and pestle or small bowl and fork
notes: Keep the liquid from the cans: it turns into a light, savory broth around the beans, which is what sets balila apart from hummus. Crushing the garlic with salt into a paste spreads its flavor evenly without raw bites. The warmed, seasoned chickpeas keep 5 days in the refrigerator and freeze well for 3 months in their liquid; add the lemon, olive oil, tomato, and parsley after reheating, not before freezing. Reheat in a saucepan with a splash of water until steaming hot (165°F). Serve with corn tortillas or rice instead of pita to make it gluten-free. Toasted pine nuts are a traditional garnish, but they add tree nuts; raw pumpkin seeds give a similar crunch and keep the bowl nut-free. A spoonful of plain whole-milk yogurt on top is also common and adds milk. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

ingredients.name: chickpeas (15 oz each), with their liquid

instructions: Tip the chickpeas with all of their liquid into a medium saucepan and add the water. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 10 minutes, until the chickpeas are very tender and hot through.

While they simmer, crush the garlic with 1/2 teaspoon of the salt in a mortar and pestle, or mince it and mash it with the salt using the flat of a knife, until it forms a smooth paste. Stir in the cumin and half the lemon juice.

Take the pan off the heat and stir the garlic mixture into the chickpeas. Lightly crush about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pan with a spoon so the liquid turns a little creamy. Taste and add salt if needed.
To prep ahead, cool the chickpeas and portion them with their liquid into containers now. Otherwise, keep them warm while you make the topping.
Toss the tomatoes and parsley with the remaining lemon juice and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt in a small bowl.

Ladle the hot chickpeas and some of their liquid into shallow bowls, drizzle each with olive oil, top with the tomato and parsley, and dust with paprika if you like. Serve with warm pita for scooping.

title: Gyeran-ppang-Style Korean Egg Breads
description: Korean street-cart egg bread made in a muffin tin: a lightly sweet, buttery batter baked with a whole egg on top. Eight portable breakfasts for about 45 cents each.
notes: Fill the cups only about a third with batter so the egg has room; a large egg in a standard cup rises close to the rim. For make-ahead breads, bake until the yolks are firm, since a runny yolk does not keep or reheat safely. Cooled breads keep 4 days in the refrigerator. To freeze, wrap each one in plastic, bag, and freeze up to 1 month; thaw overnight in the refrigerator and warm in the microwave for 30 to 40 seconds, or in a 350°F oven for 8 minutes, until hot in the center (165°F). A tablespoon of shredded low-moisture mozzarella or a few pieces of diced deli turkey breast under each egg is a common street-stall variation; neither changes the allergens. Refrigerate within 2 hours of baking.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, softened, for the tin

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Butter 8 cups of a standard 12-cup muffin tin generously, including the rims.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt in a medium bowl. In a measuring cup, whisk the milk, melted butter, 1 of the eggs, and the vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and whisk just until no dry flour remains; a few small lumps are fine. The batter should be thick but pourable.
Divide the batter among the 8 buttered cups, about 2 1/2 tablespoons each, so each is about one-third full. Crack one of the remaining eggs onto the batter in each cup.
Season the eggs with the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt and a little pepper, and scatter with parsley if using.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the bread is golden and springs back at the edges and the egg whites are fully set. For make-ahead breads, bake until the yolks are firm when gently pressed.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, run a thin knife around each one, and lift them onto a wire rack. Eat warm, or cool completely before refrigerating or freezing.

title: Masoor Dal Chilla: Savory Red Lentil Breakfast Pancakes
description: Soaked red lentils blended with ginger, chile, and turmeric into a batter that cooks into thin, crisp-edged pancakes. A protein-rich vegan breakfast that freezes well, about 50 cents a serving.
notes: Soak the lentils for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator; that soak is what lets them blend into a smooth batter, and it makes this a good recipe to start the night before. The batter keeps 2 days in the refrigerator; it thickens as it sits, so stir in water a tablespoon at a time until it pours like heavy cream. Cooked chillas keep 4 days refrigerated. To freeze, cool them on a rack, stack with parchment between, and freeze in a bag up to 2 months; reheat from frozen in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes per side, or microwave 30 to 45 seconds, until hot through (165°F). Serve with ketchup, a spoon of tomato salsa, or plain whole-milk yogurt, which adds milk. Many Indian cooks add asafoetida, but most brands contain wheat flour, so check the label if you need the recipe gluten-free. Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking.

ingredients.name: dried split red lentils (300 g), rinsed
fresh ginger (1 inch), peeled and chopped

instructions: Cover the rinsed lentils with 3 inches of cool water in a medium bowl and soak for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator, until they crush easily between your fingers. Drain well in a fine-mesh strainer.

Put the drained lentils, ginger, chile, and 1 cup water in a blender and blend until very smooth, 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down once. The batter should pour like heavy cream; add water a tablespoon at a time if it is too thick.
Pour the batter into the bowl and stir in the cumin seeds, turmeric, salt, onion, and cilantro.
Heat a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat and brush with about 1/2 teaspoon oil. Ladle in 1/3 cup batter and quickly spread it with the back of the ladle in a spiral into a 7-inch round.
Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edge and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the top looks dry and the underside is golden with crisp edges. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until spotted brown.
Move to a wire rack or plate and repeat with the remaining batter, oiling the pan each time and lowering the heat if the chillas brown before the centers set. You should get about 12.
Serve hot, or cool completely before stacking with parchment for the refrigerator or freezer.
